citation: Letellier-Duchesne, S. and Leroy, L. (2020), archetypal: A Python package for collecting, simulating, converting and analyzing building archetypes, Journal of Open Source Software, doi:10.21105/joss.01833
description: archetypal is a Python package for retrieving, building, simulating, converting and analysing building energy archetypes, the representative models used in urban building energy modelling. It was written by Samuel Letellier-Duchesne and Louis Leroy at Polytechnique Montréal and described in the Journal of Open Source Software. It works with EnergyPlus input files, converts them to TRNSYS TrnBuild multizone models and reduces them to templates for the Urban Modeling Interface (UMI) of MIT's Sustainable Design Lab, so archetype libraries need not be rebuilt by hand for each platform. Coverage: any building stock represented by EnergyPlus models. Access: source on GitHub, packages on PyPI (version 2.18.10 released 10 February 2026) and documentation on Read the Docs; the 2020 v1.3.2 release is archived on Zenodo. Licence: MIT; free, although TRNSYS itself is commercial. Caveats: the README now says archetypal will get only limited maintenance and will narrow to IDF complexity reduction for UMI templates, with new work moving to its successor idfkit. Simulation uses are urban-scale building energy models for retrofit and energy planning scenarios and archetype libraries for stock models. Related records: EnergyPlus and building stock archetype datasets.
